items.reason: Recommend reject as a British act: the protest is British High Commission note 020/4 of 4 Aug 1980 to Malaysia against the 1979 map's shelf limits and Louisa Reef (Haller-Trost 1994 p. 38 fn 198; Dzurek 1996 p. 21), with no recorded part for the Sultanate's government, and decision 03 (2026-11-23) counts only the Sultanate's own acts as Brunei's, British acts for Brunei being colonial context. If the maintainer counts it anyway it is a new move (novelty): the first protest at a rival's claim map after a 1979 of nothing; ev-8f767ab50d follows its fate.

Provisional continuation of ev-42c20f440e (1980 is a candidate of this run): a second British High Commission note (177/2, 26 May 1981) repeating the same objection to the same map, same method and target - likely reject with the note, or rejected with its lead if 1980 is judged a British act.

The Sultanate's own legislation (Fishery Limits Act 5 of 1983, in force 1 Jan 1983) claims a 200-nm or median-line fishery zone where Brunei had none, across the shelf Malaysia's 1979 map allots to itself and enclosing Louisa Reef: a new method of advancing the claim. Lead of the 1983 package; the 12-nm Territorial Waters Act (ev-121d192829) belongs with it. Note the Act has no Sabah lateral - that is the 1988 Order.

Territorial Waters of Brunei Act (9 of 1983, in force 10 Feb 1983), the 12-nm sea enacted five weeks after the fishery limits: the second statute of the one 1983 extension of Brunei's maritime zones, so one move with the fishery act as lead rather than a second intensification.

Provisional continuation of ev-118a6c3d04: the 1984 Revised Edition of the Laws republishes the Interpretation and General Clauses Act (enactment 5 of 1959, whose 'includes the continental shelf' wording carries no 1984 amendment marker, CommonLII Cap. 4) and ties 'territorial waters' to the 1983 Act (S 6/84); a consolidation of the 1983 zones at the same level, nothing new - likely reject.

Provisional continuation of ev-118a6c3d04: the Surveyor General's 1987 Sheet 1 is the map section 3 of the 1983 Territorial Waters Act requires, giving seven coordinates for the 12-nm limit already enacted; a restricted-circulation implementation map that claims no new area (Haller-Trost 1994 pp. 2-4) - likely reject. The claim-making maps are the 1988 Sheets 2 and 3 (ev-cef7d9f601).

Sheets 2 and 3 of 1988 fix Brunei's shelf and fishery limits by coordinates and push the shelf from the 100-fathom line (and the 1981 median-line assumption) to a 265-nm line north of Rifleman Bank, enclosing Louisa Reef, Owen Shoal and Rifleman Bank/Bombay Castle (Haller-Trost 1994 pp. 4-5, 38, fn 250; Dzurek 1996 p. 45): a claim over a broader area than any previous year. The fishery-limits map is given legal force by the Fishery Limits Order S 13/88 of 28 May 1988.

The Sultan's Exclusive Economic Zone Proclamation of 20 Jul 1993 (gazetted 26 Mar 1994; the 21 Jul in Haller-Trost and Roach is the press release) is Brunei's first EEZ: sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the water column to 200 nm, the last South China Sea littoral to claim one (Dzurek 1996 p. 28), with article 9 saving the 1988 shelf claim beyond. A new method against 1992, when Brunei did nothing; same 200-nm area as the 1988 fishery limits, so not scope.

In 2003 Brunei met Malaysia's January counter-licensing of Blocks L and M by signing the Block J production-sharing agreement with Total on 10 Mar 2003 (Total release, SEC 6-K; the 'April' in Energy News Bulletin is wrong) and, in March, by sending a patrol craft to drive Murphy Oil's drillship out of the area (Straits Times/FEER 3 Jul 2003; AFP 14 Jul 2003): the first Bruneian naval enforcement against a rival's licensee, a new method. The blocks themselves were awarded in Feb 2002, a year this run has no candidate for.

Recommend reject: the 16 Mar 2009 Exchange of Letters is a negotiated delimitation with Malaysia to 200 nm plus a commercial arrangement area and Malaysian transit rights (Roach 2014 p. 38; Brunei's CLCS preliminary information para. 10) - a cooperative act, excluded by the guide (section 4); its texts are unpublished, no coordinates were deposited, and no source frames it as directed at China or Vietnam.

Preliminary information received by the UN on 12 May 2009 (the day before the SPLOS/183 deadline) claims a continental shelf beyond 200 nm across the Dangerous Grounds to the deep basin, inside China's nine-dash line and Vietnam's Spratly claim, 'without prejudice' to delimitation: Brunei's first formal filing of its shelf claim with an international body, a new method (the 1988 map was domestic and restricted). No full submission ever followed and no state reacted (Roach 2014 p. 38).

Recommend reject under guide section D: the 20 Jul 2020 MFA statement (mfa.gov.bn Press Room 841) is process only - two-step approach, bilateral settlement under UNCLOS, restraint, COC - and asserts no Bruneian right, zone or feature and names no state. The alternative reading is novelty: it is the first stand-alone MFA press release on the South China Sea in the Press Room's record (2005 on), issued a week after the US position of 13 Jul 2020; the 2016 response to the award was only a deputy minister's interview.

The 2 Sep 2023 MFA statement (Press Room 1067), five days after China's standard map, adds two legal propositions absent in 2020: delimitation only under UNCLOS procedures, and maritime entitlements 'governed exclusively by international law, in particular UNCLOS' - the formula that denies dashed-line and historic-rights entitlements, aimed at China without naming it. A new method for Brunei, and in any case new again after no unilateral statement in 2021 or 2022; none has followed to Nov 2026.
